Step 11 complete. Summary:

## Step 11 — Polish + design/accessibility audit ✅

Ran the **web-design-guidelines** skill and audited the built `dist/` HTML + CSS against the Web Interface Guidelines. Findings fixed:

**Contrast (the biggest find).** In the light theme, three accents failed WCAG AA (4.5:1) for the small metadata/labels/links/chips that use them: clay (articles, ~3.4:1), ochre (reviews, ~3.2:1), and gold (~3.2:1). Darkened them within the same hue family to AA on **both** paper tones — clay `#9c4d34` (5.20/4.75), ochre+gold `#7a6122` (5.14/4.70). Oxblood, taupe, and every dark-theme accent already passed.

**Heading hierarchy.** Two separate multiple-`<h1>` bugs: section indexes emitted the nameplate `<h1>` plus the section `<h1>` (fixed by a new BaseLayout `section` variant that keeps the full nameplate visual but drops its heading role), and newsletter posts emitted up to nine `<h1>` from `#` in-issue headers (fixed by a `remark-demote-headings` plugin). Every built page now has exactly one `<h1>` except the `/blog` redirect stub.

**Other fixes:** global `:focus-visible` outline (links used `color:inherit`, so keyboard focus was invisible), a skip-to-content link, `prefers-reduced-motion` handling, `color-scheme: light/dark`, and bumped footer touch targets to ≥24px.

**Confirmed clean:** RSS feed uses plural section paths; OG + Twitter meta present on post pages with Cloudinary OG images.

**Added dependency:** `@astrojs/sitemap` (runtime) → `dist/sitemap-index.xml` emitted.

**Verification:** `vitest` 34/34, `astro check` 0 errors, `npm run build` green, sitemap present, all contrast ratios recomputed ≥4.5:1.

- Commit `f9e68f4` (+ plan/PR-checklist commit `1e96122`), pushed.
- CI: passed — https://github.com/rodmachen/edition-rodmachen-com/actions/runs/27399871696
- Result JSON written to `docs/implementation/edition-rebuild-and-rodmachen-home/results/step-11.json`.

One thing worth flagging for your judgment: the heading-demotion plugin slightly shrinks the newsletter in-issue section headers (former content `<h1>` → `<h2>`). It's an accessibility necessity, but if you want those section headers visually larger again, that's a one-line tweak to the post-body `h2` rule.
